# Test Fixtures

Each subdirectory is one self-contained test case named `<N>_<name>/`.

## Files in every fixture

| File | Purpose | Regeneratable? |
|---|---|---|
| `<name>_data.xlsx` | The source Excel file the engine extracts data from. This is the primary input used in tests. | No — it defines the test case |
| `<name>_data-cdr.xlsx` | A copy of `data.xlsx` processed by Content Disarm and Reconstruct (CDR) tooling (OPSWAT MetaDefender). Macros, VBA, and external links are stripped; the file is then reconstructed from safe content only. Used to test the security layer on files that came from untrusted sources. | No — produced by external CDR tool |
| `<name>_pattern-from-draft.xlsx` | The pattern file generated by `grepxcel draft` (LLM-assisted drafter). The `.xlsx` and `.csv` twins below always contain **identical content** in different formats — the engine accepts both and tests cover both. Regenerate with `grepxcel draft <name>_data.xlsx`. | Yes — `grepxcel draft` |
| `<name>_pattern-from-draft.csv` | CSV twin of the above. Same extraction instructions, human-readable and diff-friendly. | Yes — `grepxcel draft` |
| `<name>_pattern-manual.xlsx` | A **hand-crafted** pattern written by the project maintainer. Present only in fixtures where the drafter's output is insufficient. **Never overwrite or delete.** Protected by CLAUDE.md. | ❌ Read-only |

## Why `.xlsx` and `.csv` for patterns?

grepxcel accepts patterns in both `.xlsx` and `.csv` format. The `pattern-from-draft.*`
twins are generated together and kept byte-identical in meaning so tests can verify
both parsers produce the same extraction result (see `test_csv_pattern_parity.py`).
